ballet.blurb: From French ballet, from Italian balletto, a diminutive of ballo 'dance'.

boondocks.blurb: From Tagalog bundok 'mountain', via US troops in the Philippines.

caravan.blurb: From Persian karvan, a company of desert travellers.

coffee.blurb: From Arabic qahwah, likely via Turkish kahve and Dutch koffie.

elapse.blurb: From Middle French, from Latin elapsus, 'to slip away' (e- + labi).

geyser.blurb: From Icelandic Geysir, the famous hot spring, from geysa 'to gush'.

guru.blurb: From Hindi guru 'teacher', from Sanskrit guru 'venerable, weighty'.

juggernaut.blurb: From Sanskrit Jagannatha, 'lord of the world', whose festival cart was said to crush devotees.

jungle.blurb: From Hindi jangal 'wilderness, forest', from Sanskrit jangala.

karaoke.blurb: Japanese kara 'empty' + oke (short for okestora) 'orchestra' — an 'empty orchestra'.

kiosk.blurb: From Turkish koshk, 'pavilion', ultimately from Persian.

malaria.blurb: Italian mala aria, 'bad air' — from the old belief about swamp vapours.

mammoth.blurb: From Russian mammut, probably from a Siberian (Mansi) source word.

orange.blurb: A long march: Sanskrit naranga -> Persian -> Arabic -> Old French orenge -> English.

paparazzi.blurb: Italian, from Fellini's La Dolce Vita (1960): the photographer Paparazzo.

pizza.blurb: From Italian pizza, popularized in the US by returning WWII soldiers.

rickshaw.blurb: Japanese jinrikisha, 'man-powered vehicle' — shortened in English.

robot.blurb: Coined in Czech (robota, 'forced labor') by Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R.

safari.blurb: From Swahili safari 'journey', from Arabic safar 'to travel'.

samovar.blurb: Russian samovar, 'self-boiler' — the tea urn of Russian tradition.

serendipity.blurb: Coined by Horace Walpole from the Persian tale of the Three Princes of Serendip (Sri Lanka).

taboo.blurb: From Tongan tabu, 'sacred, forbidden', also via Cook's voyages.

tattoo.blurb: From Tahitian tatau, recorded on Cook's voyages.

tea.blurb: Via Dutch thee from Min Nan Chinese te — the 'te' branch of the word's world map.

they.blurb: Old Norse their — one of the pronouns borrowed wholesale from Norse.

tycoon.blurb: Japanese taikun, 'great lord' — the shogun's title, later applied to US magnates.

typhoon.blurb: From Cantonese taai fung 'great wind', blended with earlier trade-wind forms.

window.blurb: Old Norse vindauga, 'wind-eye' — replacing Old English eagduru.

yogurt.blurb: From Turkish yogurt, perhaps related to yogun 'thick'.
